newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul blue chips seen rising; others consolidating.
newsitem.headline: Seoul blue chips seen rising; others consolidating.

text.p: Blue chips are expected to gain ahead of the May 2 increase in the foreign shareholding ceiling, but other shares will be mixed or weaker on consolidation, brokers said on Monday.
Sunday's arrival in Seoul of North Korean defector Hwang Jang-yop is barely seen impacting the stock market, they said.
"Blue chips will be firmer in general ahead of the rise in the foreign ownership ceiling," said Lee Kye-joon of Daishin Securities.
The index ended 4.98 points higher at 700.65 on Saturday.
The ceiling is due to rise to 23 percent of a listed company's outstanding shares from the current 20 percent.
The planned ceiling expansion has been boosting buying in blue-chip shares that are believed to be favoured by foreign investors, brokers said.

Hwang Jang-yop, the highest North Korean official ever to defect the communist state, arrived in Seoul on Sunday more than two months after he sought political asylum in Seoul's mission in Beijing in February.
